clos.description: Explain fundamental concepts of data science, including data collection, cleaning, and visualization.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Direct instruction (lecture), Guided discussion, Case examples
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Written quizzes, concept tests, in-class participation

clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Coding exercises, lab assignments, practical test

clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Collaborative learning, Group projects, Case study discussions

topics.title: What is Data Science?
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the concept of data science and its role in solving real-world problems. LLO2: Distinguish data science from related fields such as IT and computer science.

topics.title: History of Data Science
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the evolution of data science from statistics and computer science to AI. LLO2: Identify key milestones and drivers behind the growth of data science.

topics.title: About Data
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Classify diverse types of data (structured, semi-structured, unstructured). LLO2: Explain common data sources and their relevance to data science applications.

topics.title: Data Privacy
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the importance of data privacy and ethical data handling. LLO2: Identify common privacy risks and data protection principles in real-world scenarios.

topics.title: Programming for Data Science
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the role of programming in data science workflows. LLO2: Apply basic programming concepts to simple data processing tasks.

topics.title: Introduction to Python (Part I)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Write basic Python programs using variables, data types, input, and output. LLO2: Apply data type conversion to solve simple computational problems.

topics.title: Introduction to Python (Part II)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply control structures (if-else, loops) and functions in Python programs. LLO2: Use basic Python libraries to perform simple data manipulation tasks.

topics.title: Midterm
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Demonstrate understanding of foundational data science concepts. LLO2: Demonstrate understanding of foundational data science concepts and Python basics.

topics.title: Reading Scientific Papers
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify the key components of a scientific research paper. LLO2: Analyze and summarize research findings using academic sources.

topics.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain fundamental machine learning concepts and learning types. LLO2: Identify appropriate machine learning approaches for simple real-world problems.

topics.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain basic deep learning concepts and neural network architectures. LLO2: Differentiate deep learning from traditional machine learning approaches.

topics.title: Where to Apply Data Science
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify major industries and domains that apply data science. LLO2: Analyze how data science solutions support decision-making in real-world contexts.

topics.title: Capstone Project
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define a real-world problem suitable for data science application. LLO2: Design a basic data science workflow to address the identified problem.

topics.title: Capstone Project
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply data science techniques to analyze a real-world dataset. LLO2: Interpret analytical results to generate meaningful insights.

topics.title: Capstone Project Presentation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Present project findings clearly using appropriate visualizations and explanations. LLO2: Demonstrate teamwork, professionalism, and ethical awareness during presentation.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
